Verification: L-201 fixed and complete. ApprovalManager::request() guards each notifyPending (report + approval_notify_failed_total{notifier}, the remaining notifiers still run). The pipeline's CapabilityApprovalRequested goes through InvokeResultFinalizer::dispatch (guarded, bus_listener_failed_total). ApprovalManager::dispatch and ApprovalExecutor's CapabilityApprovalExecuted dispatch and approval audit were already guarded, so nothing between the saved row and finishApprovalRequired can now turn it into internal. L-202 fixed and complete. The second writer is gone from the manager, the executor, the constructor args and the helpers, with no remaining callers in any package. The provider and registry executors both route through CapabilityRegistry::executeApproval (original requester, the original key, executing_approval_id), so the pipeline is the only writer. storeResult keeps the approval_id from the settled pending_approval row. An expired-row claim resets approval_id to null in both stores, so no stale id is inherited. The follow-on conflict/busy fix is correct: lookup refusals null state->idempotencyKey, so finishFailure never writes the owner's row. finishUncaught after a successful claim still stores failed. Hash stability across the approval round-trip holds because RequestHash canonicalizes (ksort), so a MySQL JSON key reorder of input_json cannot cause a false conflict on execution. The X-203 CHANGELOG claims match the code (the removed helpers are absent; ArtisanCommandRegistrar::infrastructure()/all() exist and the provider uses all()). Checked and not raised: (a) the approval-execution-meets-processing-row race is still ms-wide; with the busy fix the approval is now marked executed/failed(conflict, retryable) instead of the row being briefly overwritten, and the window is unchanged from what iteration 3 dismissed. (b) The approved-execution-after-idempotency-TTL-expiry corner (the claim creates a fresh processing row; a crash mid-run then makes resume answer busy) needs TTL expiry plus a crash, and both TTLs default to 24h. (c) The notifier metric label uses $notifier::class, which is ugly only for anonymous classes (tests). (d) Rate-limited or authorize refusals after a successful claim replay as failed for the TTL, which is D-005's documented default 'replay failure'. (e) ApprovalMetrics is in-process and separate from the container Metrics sink; this predates these changes and is test-facing.
